title: Design a Voltage Regulator Using Zener Diode in MATLAB/Simulink

questions.q: Why is a Zener regulator called a shunt regulator?
questions.a: Because the regulating Zener diode is connected in parallel (shunt) with the load resistor RL.

questions.q: Why must the Zener diode be connected in reverse bias in Experiment 12?
questions.a: Because Zener voltage regulation occurs at the reverse breakdown voltage Vz (e.g., 5.1 V). In forward bias, it behaves like an ordinary diode with a 0.7 V drop.

questions.q: How do you determine if the Zener diode is in breakdown (regulating) for given V_in, Rs, and RL?
questions.a: Calculate the voltage divider voltage without the Zener: V_th = V_in * RL / (Rs + RL). If V_th > Vz, the Zener is in breakdown and V_out = Vz.

questions.q: What happens if series resistor Rs is removed from the Zener regulator?
questions.a: The voltage source V_in is connected directly across the Zener diode with nothing to drop (V_in - Vz), causing infinite/destructive current through the Zener.

questions.q: What is the minimum input voltage V_in_min required for a 5.1 V Zener to regulate with Rs = 220 Ω and RL = 1 kΩ?
How do you orient a reverse-biased Zener diode at Node 2 in PySpice?
questions.a: `circuit.Diode('Z1', circuit.gnd, 2, model='DZ5V1')` — anode at `circuit.gnd` and cathode at Node `2`.

questions.q: Which components share Node 2 (the regulated output node) in Experiment 12?
questions.a: Series resistor Rs (from Node 1), Zener cathode DZ1 (to GND), and load resistor RL (to GND).

questions.q: For V_in = 12 V, Vz = 5.1 V, Rs = 220 Ω, and RL = 1 kΩ, calculate I_s, I_L, and I_Z.
If your simulation shows V_out = 0.7 V instead of 5.1 V, what is wrong?
questions.a: The Zener diode anode and cathode are reversed (connected in forward bias instead of reverse bias).

questions.q: What happens to Zener current I_Z if the load resistor RL is disconnected (open load)?
questions.a: I_L drops to 0, so the entire series current I_s (31.36 mA) flows through the Zener diode.
